title: How To Cut Your Preparation Time And Lower Stress
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Facing the added prep burden of pandemic-era teaching, Linsin recommends the Pomodoro Technique, a time-management method created by Francesco Cirillo, as a way to shorten prep tasks while producing better results. He describes the mechanics simply: work in focused 25-minute blocks (pomodoros) followed by five-minute breaks, with a longer 30-minute break after every four pomodoros, and includes practical tips like never working through a break and protecting each block from interruption. He explains the technique's effectiveness through Parkinson's Law — the tendency of a task to expand to fill the time allotted — arguing that a hard time limit prevents overthinking and produces sharper, less labored work. He adds that the method compounds over time, training teachers to become faster and more focused rather than just producing a one-time efficiency boost.
points: Use the Pomodoro Technique: work in focused 25-minute blocks followed by 5-minute breaks.
Take a longer break of at least 30 minutes after every four pomodoros.
Never work during a break — the break's purpose is genuine recovery, not more task-switching.
The technique counters Parkinson's Law, the tendency for a task to expand to fill whatever time is allotted to it.
Over time, the method trains you to become faster, sharper, and more focused, not just more efficient in the moment.
quotes: In the late 1980s, an Italian software developer named Francesco Cirillo created a way to shorten work-related tasks while producing better results.
Set a timer for 25 minutes. This block of time is called a pomodoro.
Protect your pomodoros at all costs. Let nothing short of emergency interrupt you.
The Pomodoro Technique works because it creates a powerful sense of urgency that is both highly motivating and maximally efficient.
Parkinson’s Law is the tendency to expand a task in complexity in relation to the time given for its completion.
Over time, however, and what is so cool about it is that it actually trains you to become smarter, faster, and more focused.
